https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/rox-data-corp/b.description: ABOUT ROX At Rox, we believe in empowering people to do their best work. We are reimagining the revenue stack by building the world's first revenue operating system — from the application layer to the system of context. This is a high-ownership, high-visibility seat that reports to and partners closely with the VP of Revenue Operations and Finance. You’ll own commission and quota planning, and you’ll be a core analytical partner on territory design and sales performance analytics. You will define the foundations that enable us to have a data driven command of our GTM, and your work will drive decisions that show up in the board deck. We’re an AI-first company, and we expect RevOps to operate that way too. You’ll be encouraged to reach for AI and automation before spreadsheets and manual process — using our own platform, agents and modern tooling to model, analyze, and report faster than a traditional ops team ever could. We’d rather you build a repeatable, AI-driven system than a one-off analysis. WHAT YOU’LL DO 1. Commission & quota planning (owner) You’ll own the analytics behind how we set quotas and how we pay for performance. That means modeling quota-setting across roles and segments, designing and pressure-testing comp plans against budget and behavior, running quota and comp scenarios for planning cycles, and administering the mechanics of the plans in partnership with Finance. You’ll lean on AI and automation to run scenarios and keep plans current in near-real time, and you’ll make sure incentives, cost of sale, and attainment all line up — and that reps and leadership trust the numbers. 2. Territory analysis & design Partnering with the VP of Revenue Operations and Finance, you’ll provide the analytical horsepower behind how we carve up the market and deploy our sellers. You instinctively reach for AI, agents, and automation to do the work faster and better, and you’re excited to build RevOps on top of Rox’s own product. - Deep comfort with quantitative modeling. You can build a comp plan, a quota model, or a territory carve from a blank spreadsheet, and you can defend every assumption in it. - Fluency in the GTM data stack — hands-on CRM experience (Salesforce or HubSpot), and comfort in a BI tool (Looker, Tableau, Sigma, or similar). You can take an ambiguous leadership question, structure it, do the analysis, and come back with a clear recommendation — not just a chart. - High ownership and low ego. You’re comfortable owning a metric and a cadence, chasing down the data, and driving a decision to close in a fast-moving environment.
